label: The wrapper launches a Claude hop with --name "<stem> (<hops+1>)"; a successful carry shows the numbered stem, not the sender's exact name.

The wrapper replays --remote-control and its optional value; the vendor does not rank --name against it, so the app title is UNCONFIRMED and the smallest change is to rewrite or drop the replayed value when a carried name exists.
A hop is a new process, so the app shows a new remote session when Remote Control is on, not the old session continuing; the old session goes offline.

A sender connected only by /remote-control leaves no launch flag to replay; the wrapper cannot re-establish Remote Control on the receiver, and no Claude session-store reader exists to supply the bridged state.

The mobile rename reading 1 remains the store-versus-transcript gap; a store-only rename is invisible to prepare, and the smallest change is a session-store reader in resolveSessionSettings beside claudeSessionLogPath.

Smallest live-run set: Run A (Claude, the three 039 fixes plus 016/L3, 008 and 012), Run B (Claude Remote Control, both mobile readings plus 039/003 in the app and the --remote-control precedence), Run C (Pi, 002 and 015), Run D (OpenCode, 005, 013 and 008), Run E (HS-8, 017/L3 and the late write if it happens).

No live run can prove 038/017/L2 (shutdown race), 038/013/L2 (fault injection), 038/010 L1 to L3 (recycled pid, spawn window, Windows), 038/003/L1 (measurement), 038/016/L1 (statistics), the model-obedience limits, 039/001 L5 and L6, 039/003 L2, 038/012/L2, or 039/002 L1 and L2.

Ranking by operator impact against cost: mobile app name (high/medium), 039/001 (high/low), 039/002 (medium-high/low), Codex goal reader (high/high), OpenCode 005 and 013 (medium/medium), Pi 002 and 015 (medium/low-medium), 038/008 (low-medium/low), 038/004 switch-off (low/low), 038/017/L3 (low/very low), the 017/013/010 races (low/high), then the 002 parent goal, phase 033 and the Commit-Id doc (low/low).

The report's "without that name" has three shapes: no name, a different name (generated or the replayed --remote-control value), or the numbered <stem> (n); Run B distinguishes them by the record's name, the receiver's launch line and the app title.
The 039/002 live run needs a goal.md with an unticked - [ ] criterion in the durable slice and budgetState ok; the harness demo goal has no checkbox, so the run must add one.
The 039/001 live run must let the sender run prepare itself and then open AskUserQuestion; the HS-8 variant already moves prepare into the sender and is the base for the patch.
The vendor's title order puts --name, --remote-control and /remote-control in one slot and does not rank them when both --name and --remote-control <name> are present.
Each interactive Claude Code process registers one remote session, so a hop's fresh process appears as a new session and the sender goes offline.
The harness demo goal has no unchecked criterion, so the packet-goal fallback live run needs a goal.md with an unticked - [ ] line and an ok budget.
A hop can continue the session name but not the session identity; the app always shows a new remote session when Remote Control is on.
A store-only mobile rename cannot reach prepare until a Claude session-store reader exists beside claudeSessionLogPath.
